People elsewhere (#393 slices 2-3): when a line names someone or somewhere elsewhere, is the narration told [whereabouts] and true to it, and does the reader offer the journey for a line that seeks them (run 6's a64)?

Dice over lines (LINE-CLAIM-OVER-THE-DICE): when a line takes for granted what the dice decided otherwise, does the narration tell what the dice made true, and how many [dice] judge calls and re-asks were made?
Openings in the second person (OPENING-IN-THE-THIRD-PERSON): is every second-person opening and spotlight told as "you", and did the [person] check re-ask any?
The fact block (SIDECAR-NOTE-IN-THE-PROSE): does any posted narration carry text written after its fact block?

The ship and the scene (SHIP-BOUND-FOR-READ-AS-NEAR, EXPEDITION-LEGS-TURN-THE-SCENE): does a narration that names a destination move the ship's record, and is each expedition one scene from its start to its arrival?
